Error collecting tests on 9.1.1 - fixtures not found when a parent directory appears multiple times in a argument list 

_Disclosure: I have used AI to investigate this issue but am able to reproduce everything locally._

In Home Assistant, we tried to upgrade from PyTest 9.0.3 to 9.1.1 in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/174371 (some diagnosis in comments)

We first ran into a collection abort issue in 9.1.0 that got fixed in 9.1.1 with https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14591.

With 9.1.1 we're hitting a new issue when collecting tests.

```

In tests/components/tts/test_init.py::test_setup_component_no_access_cache_folder: function uses no argument 'init_tts_cache_dir_side_effect'
```

I / Claude were not able to get a reproduction going outside of HA, so to reproduce you need to set up a HA dev env.

Step 1: Get a Home Assistant dev environment.

```
gh repo clone home-assistant/core
cd core
script/setup
```

```
> uv pip freeze | grep pytest
pytest==9.0.3

```

Step 2: Test collection passes

```

  tests/test_config_entries.py \
  tests/components/tts/test_init.py
```

Step 3: upgrade to pytest 9.1.1


Expand below to get a more elaborate AI generated description of the issue

<details>
<summary>AI generated diagnosis</summary>

### Description

In pytest 9.1 (both 9.1.0 and 9.1.1), the computed fixture closure of a test can change depending on **which unrelated paths were collected before it**. When a test relies on *implicit indirect* parametrization — `@pytest.mark.parametrize("some_fixture", [...])` where the test depends on `some_fixture` only transitively, not as a direct argument — collecting certain unrelated directories first causes that fixture to drop out of the closure, and collection fails with:

```
function uses no argument 'some_fixture'
```

The same test collects fine when run on its own, or when the other paths are collected in a different order. This passes on 9.0.3 and fails on 9.1.x, so it's a regression. I believe it is related to the fixture override-precedence rework (#14513 / PR #14566), which changed override ordering from registration-order to visibility/scope-order.

A test's fixture closure should be independent of what unrelated paths were collected earlier in the session.

### Reproduction

This reproduces against the public Home Assistant repo (the fixture graph that triggers it is non-trivial; I have not yet reduced it to a standalone `conftest.py`, but the repro below is fully deterministic and takes three commands):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/home-assistant/core hass-core
cd hass-core
git checkout 957c24fcd724          # any recent dev commit works
python -m venv venv && . venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements_test.txt -r requirements.txt   # or: pip install -e . pytest-aiohttp syrupy ...
pip install pytest==9.1.1

# Order matters. This fails:
pytest --collect-only \
  tests/components/water_heater \
  tests/test_config_entries.py \
  tests/components/tts/test_init.py
```

**Actual (9.1.1):**

```
ERROR collecting tests/components/tts/test_init.py
In tests/components/tts/test_init.py::test_setup_component_no_access_cache_folder: function uses no argument 'init_tts_cache_dir_side_effect'
!!! Interrupted: 1 error during collection !!!
```

**Expected (and actual on 9.0.3):** clean collection, ~3.6k tests collected, no error.

Notes on determinism:
- Deterministic across `PYTHONHASHSEED` (fails on random seeds and on fixed seeds 0–5).
- The failing file passes in isolation: `pytest --collect-only tests/components/tts/test_init.py` ✅.
- Reversing the order (e.g. collecting `tts` first) also passes — it is purely the order in which the earlier paths are collected.
- `--collect-only` is enough; no xdist required (we originally hit it under `-n auto --dist=loadfile`, but it's not xdist-specific).

### Why the test is structured this way (for context)

`tests/components/tts/test_init.py::test_setup_component_no_access_cache_folder`:

```python
@pytest.mark.parametrize("init_tts_cache_dir_side_effect", [OSError(2, "No access")])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("setup", ["mock_setup", "mock_config_entry_setup"], indirect=True)
async def test_setup_component_no_access_cache_folder(
    hass, mock_tts_init_cache_dir, setup
):
    ...
```

The closure that makes the `init_tts_cache_dir_side_effect` parametrize valid:

- the test directly requests `mock_tts_init_cache_dir` (in `tests/components/conftest.py`)
- `mock_tts_init_cache_dir` → requests `init_tts_cache_dir_side_effect` (also `tests/components/conftest.py`)
- additionally, `tests/components/tts/conftest.py` has an **autouse fixture that overrides a parent fixture and requests the same-named super**:
  ```python
  @pytest.fixture(autouse=True, name="mock_tts_cache_dir")
  def mock_tts_cache_dir_fixture_autouse(mock_tts_cache_dir):  # requests the parent of the same name
      return mock_tts_cache_dir
  ```
  whose parent (`tests/components/conftest.py`) transitively also reaches `init_tts_cache_dir_side_effect`.

Under 9.1 with a triggering prefix, `init_tts_cache_dir_side_effect` is no longer present in the closure, even though `mock_tts_init_cache_dir` is still requested directly — which is what makes this look like a closure-computation bug tied to the new override ordering rather than intended behavior.

### Environment

- pytest 9.1.1 (also reproduces on 9.1.0); **last known good: 9.0.3**
- pluggy 1.6.0
- Python 3.14.5
- macOS (Darwin arm64); also seen on Linux CI (Python 3.14.5)

### Suspected cause

#14513 / PR #14566 — fixture override ordering changed from registration-order to visibility-order. The order-dependence of the closure is the smell: with the new ordering, resolving an overridden fixture for the tts test appears to pick a fixturedef that no longer carries the `init_tts_cache_dir_side_effect` dependency, depending on what was registered while collecting earlier paths.

### Related

- #14591 — separate 9.1.0 regression ("duplicate parametrization of '<arg>'" when a fixture has `params=` and a test re-parametrizes it with `indirect=True`), fixed in 9.1.1. This report is a *different* problem that 9.1.1 does not fix.

</details>

problem_statement:
DEFAULT_CONFIG declares "kanban" twice; the auto_subscribe_on_create default is silently dropped

### What happens

`DEFAULT_CONFIG` declares the `"kanban"` key twice, so the first block is silently dropped and the `auto_subscribe_on_create` default is missing from `DEFAULT_CONFIG`.

```python
from hermes_cli.config import DEFAULT_CONFIG
"auto_subscribe_on_create" in DEFAULT_CONFIG["kanban"]   # -> False
```

### Where

`hermes_cli/config.py`, `DEFAULT_CONFIG`:

- First block: `"kanban": {"auto_subscribe_on_create": True}`
- Later block: `"kanban": {"dispatch_in_gateway": True, "dispatch_interval_seconds": 60, ...}`

Python keeps only the last literal for a duplicate key, so the first block (and its `auto_subscribe_on_create` default) is discarded.

### Impact

`tools/kanban_tools.py` reads the value with `cfg_get(cfg, "kanban", "auto_subscribe_on_create", default=True)`, so the hardcoded fallback masks the missing default at runtime today. But:
- The documented default is absent from `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, so config templates and `hermes config show` omit it.
- The duplicate key is a latent hazard: any future key added to the first block would also silently disappear.

### Expected

A single `kanban` block in `DEFAULT_CONFIG` that carries every documented default, including `auto_subscribe_on_create`.

A fix with regression tests is in #55778.

problem_statement:
Feature: expose tool_call_history in subagent_stop hook payload

## Problem

The `subagent_stop` shell hook currently receives:
- `child_summary` (self-reported narrative text)
- `child_status`, `child_role`, `child_task`, `duration_ms`

It does **not** include the child agent's actual `tool_call_history` — the list of tool invocations the subagent made. This means:

1. **Narrative Override attacks** cannot be definitively detected. A subagent can claim "wrote report.json" in its summary but actually have written to a different file, or performed undisclosed operations.
2. **Governance layers cannot validate** assertions in child_summary against ground truth (actual tool calls).
3. **Audit completeness** is limited — hooks are blind to what the subagent actually *did*.

## Impact

Governance/adversarial-review hooks must trust the subagent's self-reported narrative (child_summary) without any way to cross-reference it against actual operations. This is a fundamental visibility gap.

## Proposed Solution

Add an optional `tool_call_history` field to the subagent_stop payload, containing a list of tool invocations made by the child agent. Each entry could include:
- `tool_name`
- `tool_input` (summary/truncated)
- `tool_output` (truncated or omitted for privacy)
- `timestamp`

This enables governance hooks to:
- Cross-reference claimed outputs in child_summary against actual file writes
- Detect undisclosed side-effects
- Compute actual operation count vs. claimed

## Current Workaround

The governance layer at `E:/work/governance/orchestrator.py` currently validates `claimed_outputs` by checking file existence on disk — but this only works for file artifacts and cannot detect operations that don't leave persistent files (network calls, variable mutations, etc.).

Gateway marks a crashed platform adapter fatal and never retries — transient upstream outage permanently kills the platform

**Version:** Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20), upstream 0ce9022e, macOS (launchd-supervised gateway).

**What happened**

The photon platform's upstream service had a transient outage (its gRPC endpoint returned UNAVAILABLE / the fronting CDN served origin-error pages). The adapter's sidecar did what it is designed to do — degraded-stream watchdog exited with code 75 so the adapter could restart it — but after repeated sidecar exits the gateway gave up permanently:

```
INFO  [photon-sidecar] photon-sidecar: upstream stream degraded for 91001ms; exiting so Hermes can restart the Photon adapter
ERROR hermes_plugins.photon_platform.adapter: [photon] sidecar exited unexpectedly (code 75) — triggering reconnect
ERROR gateway.run: Fatal photon adapter error (SIDECAR_CRASHED): Photon sidecar exited unexpectedly (code 75)
```

After the `Fatal photon adapter error` line there were no further reconnect attempts of any kind. The upstream service recovered minutes later, but the platform stayed dead inside the still-running gateway for ~17.5 hours until a manual `hermes gateway start`. The gateway itself was healthy the whole time (other platforms kept working), so nothing signaled that one platform had been silently amputated. Cron jobs with `--deliver photon` logged `delivery error: Photon standalone send failed: All connection attempts failed` on every delivery in the window.

**Expected**

A platform adapter that dies on a *transient upstream* failure should be revived: exponential-backoff retry, or a periodic revive probe (even every 10–15 minutes would have cut this outage from 17.5h to minutes), or at minimum a loud persistent signal in `gateway status` that a configured platform is in a fatal state.

**Repro sketch**

1. Run the gateway with a platform whose sidecar exits when its upstream is unreachable (photon behaves this way by design).
2. Block the upstream long enough for the crash-loop to hit the fatal threshold.
3. Unblock the upstream. The adapter never comes back; `gateway status` shows the gateway healthy.

problem_statement:
Bug: hermes update breaks stock macOS when uv entrypoint requires realpath

## Bug description

On a stock macOS installation, `hermes update` can leave the `hermes` command unusable because uv-generated venv entrypoints invoke the external `realpath` command. macOS does not ship `realpath` by default.

## Reproduction

1. Use macOS without Homebrew/coreutils and with no `realpath` on `PATH`.
2. Install Hermes through the standard git/uv installer.
3. Run `hermes update`.
4. Run `hermes` or `hermes update` again.

## Actual behavior

The generated entrypoint contains:

```sh
'''exec' "$(dirname -- "$(realpath -- "$0")")"/'python3' "$0" "$@"
```

It fails with `realpath: command not found`, then resolves the wrong Python path. A follow-up `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'` is misleading: PyYAML is present in the venv but the launcher no longer reaches that interpreter.

## Expected behavior

The standard macOS installation and `hermes update` should work without requiring Homebrew/coreutils or a system-wide `realpath` command.

## Proposed fix

Avoid the uv-generated console script in the user-facing launcher. In `scripts/install.sh` (`setup_path`), for venv installs launch the checked-in entrypoint through the venv interpreter instead:

```sh
exec "$INSTALL_DIR/venv/bin/python" "$INSTALL_DIR/hermes" "$@"
```

This preserves venv dependencies, bypasses the `realpath` dependency entirely, and is recreated correctly by every update.

## Verification

I verified the proposed command in an environment whose `PATH` excluded `realpath`; `hermes --version` completed successfully.

## Temporary workaround

A user-local `~/.local/bin/realpath` shim works, but the launcher change above avoids imposing that workaround on every macOS user.

## Environment

- macOS 12.7.6 (Intel)
- Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)
- uv 0.11.11

problem_statement:
[Bug]: `hermes skills update` silently replaces skills with same-named ones from a different registry (data loss)

### What happened

`hermes skills update` (no args) reported a clean success:

```
Updated 4 skill(s).
```

In reality it replaced two skills with **same-named skills from a different registry by different authors**, deleting the originals' scripts. The lockfile's `source` was silently rewritten.

| Skill | Before (`clawhub`) | After (`skills.sh`) | Damage |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stock-market-pro` | 8 files incl. `scripts/{yf,news,uw,options_links,ddg_search}.py` | **1 file** (`SKILL.md`) | all 5 scripts deleted; the new `SKILL.md` still instructs `uv run --script scripts/yf price [TICKER]` → **self-referentially broken** |
| `reddit` | `scripts/reddit.mjs`, `skill-card.md`, `_meta.json`, `.clawhub/origin.json` | another author's README/SKILL.md | `reddit.mjs` deleted; the install was then blocked mid-flight by the security scanner, leaving a **half-swapped tree** |

The lockfile diff is the diagnostic fingerprint:

```diff
-  "source": "clawhub",              +  "source": "skills.sh",
-  "identifier": "stock-market-pro"  +  "identifier": "skills-sh/sundial-org/awesome-openclaw-skills/stock-market-pro"
-  "files": [8 entries]              +  "files": ["SKILL.md"]
```

### Why it's hard to notice

`hermes skills check` afterwards reports `up_to_date` — it faithfully tracks the *new* upstream. Nothing in the CLI surfaces that you're now running a different author's code. Only a file-level diff reveals it. Recovery was only cheap because `~/.hermes` happened to be a git repo.

### Root cause

Two independent defects, either of which is sufficient:

**1. `tools/skills_hub.py::check_for_skill_updates`** — the candidate-source list falls back to *every* registry when the recorded source has no adapter:

```python
candidate_sources = [src for src in sources if _source_matches(src, source_name)] or sources
```

Skill names are not namespaced across registries, so a same-named skill elsewhere satisfies `src.fetch(identifier)` and is reported as *this* entry's update.

**2. `hermes_cli/skills_hub.py::do_update`** — passes the identifier to `do_install` with no source constraint:

```python
do_install(entry["identifier"], category=category, force=True, console=c)
```

When the identifier is bare (no slash, e.g. `reddit`), `do_install` sends it through `_resolve_short_name`'s fuzzy catalog search across all sources, which picks a foreign-registry match and installs it.

`reddit` shows both interacting: the resolver picked `theglove44/reddit` from skills.sh, the security scanner then hard-blocked the install (same `export REDDIT_PASSWORD=` false positive as #59010's neighbourhood) — but **files had already been overwritten before the scan gate**, so a blocked install is not atomic.

### Expected behaviour

An update should never change a skill's source registry. A cross-registry move is a *provenance change*, not an update.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent `v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)`, macOS 26.5.2 arm64
- Affected skills sourced from `clawhub`, hijacked by `skills.sh`'s `sundial-org/awesome-openclaw-skills` mirror

### Related

Same `do_update` → `do_install(bare_name)` → `_resolve_short_name` path as the resolver problems in #6866 and #37008, but with a data-destructive outcome rather than a no-op or hang.

I have a fix + regression tests and will open a PR referencing this issue.

save_env_value writes unquoted values with internal spaces - breaks shell-sourcing of .env (core-writer sibling of #57247)

## Impact (first)

Real flows write **filesystem paths that routinely contain spaces** into `~/.hermes/.env` via the core writer `save_env_value` → `_quote_env_value`:

| Flow | Env key | Source |
|------|---------|--------|
| `hermes setup` → SSH backend | `TERMINAL_SSH_KEY` | `hermes_cli/setup.py` (~1416) `save_env_value("TERMINAL_SSH_KEY", ssh_key)` |
| Google Chat setup | `GOOGLE_CHAT_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` | `plugins/platforms/google_chat/adapter.py` (~3484) |
| `hermes config set TERMINAL_SSH_KEY …` / `terminal.ssh_key` | same / via terminal env bridge | `set_config_value` → `save_env_value` (`hermes_cli/config.py`) |

**macOS is most exposed**: paths under `~/Library/Application Support/...` are common for keys and service-account JSON. Windows `Program Files` / user profile spaces are also in-scope when those paths are saved through the same writer.

## Repro (upstream/main @ `bcea5371c`)

Throwaway `HERMES_HOME`, real `save_env_value`:

```text
value = /Users/paulo/Library/Application Support/hermes/keys/id_ed25519
```

**Emitted line (verbatim):**
```text
TERMINAL_SSH_KEY=/Users/paulo/Library/Application Support/hermes/keys/id_ed25519
```

**python-dotenv:** OK — returns the full path (masks the bug for Hermes runtime load).

**Shell source:**
```bash
env -i sh -c 'set -a; . file; set +a'
```
**Exact error:**
```text
.env: line 1: Support/hermes/keys/id_ed25519: No such file or directory
```
(`TERMINAL_SSH_KEY` ends up empty / truncated after word-split.)

## Trigger condition (line numbers on this base)

`hermes_cli/config.py` `_quote_env_value` @ **7772**, used by `save_env_value` @ **7788**:

```python
needs_quoting = (
    "#" in value
    or '"' in value
    or "'" in value
    or value != value.strip()
)
```

Internal whitespace (space/tab between non-space characters) does **not** trigger quoting. Only `#`, quotes, or leading/trailing whitespace do.

## Why python-dotenv masks it

`python-dotenv` / `dotenv_values` treat unquoted values as running to EOL (modulo `#` comments). Shell `.` / `source` with `set -a` does POSIX word-splitting on unquoted assignment RHS / bare path fragments after the first space — so tools that shell-source `.env` (debug scripts, containers, `set -a; . ~/.hermes/.env`) break while Hermes itself keeps working.

## Class link (honest)

| Item | Surface | Status |
|------|---------|--------|
| **#57247** (accepted) | Installer writer for `AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` | Bug accepted |
| **#57249** | Fixes **only** the installer (`install.sh` / `install.ps1`) | Does **not** touch `hermes_cli/config.py` |
| **#57449** | Competing installer-only PR | Same installer surface; **not** core serializer |
| **This issue** | **Core serializer** `_quote_env_value` / `save_env_value` | Sibling class: same unquoted-spaced-path failure mode, different write path |

#57249 is the right dialect (`\\` then `\"` then wrap) already used by `_quote_env_value`; the gap is the **trigger** missing internal whitespace, not the escape algorithm.

## Platform statement

- **Reproduced** on macOS with a real spaced path under Application Support.
- Failure mode is **POSIX shell sourcing**, not Hermes' primary dotenv load path.
- Fix is portable: quote when `any(c.isspace() for c in value)`; no install-script changes (those remain #57249's surface).

## Expected fix

Extend `needs_quoting` only (escaping/wrapping **unchanged**). Idempotent re-save; no mass-requote of unrelated `.env` keys on next write of a different key.

A UTF-16 .env silently corrupts the first key - and the sanitizer writes the corruption back to disk

## Impact

Saving `~/.hermes/.env` as **Unicode (UTF-16 LE + BOM)** from Windows Notepad (or any editor that writes UTF-16) causes Hermes to **silently drop the first env key** and then **permanently rewrite the on-disk file in a mangled form**.

- No error is raised.
- Canonical `os.environ.get("HERMES_TEST_KEY")` returns `None`.
- The first key appears under a mangled name like `\ufffd\ufffdHERMES_TEST_KEY`.
- On the next startup, the sanitizer has already rewritten the file with U+FFFD bytes baked in (`EF BF BD EF BF BD...`), so the corruption **survives** even if the user later opens the file in a UTF-8 editor.

This is worse than a pure load bug: the pre-load sanitizer **persists** the damage.

## Byte-level repro (macOS / Linux; emulates Notepad "Unicode")

Against current `main` (`bcea5371c`):

```python
import codecs, os, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from hermes_cli.env_loader import load_hermes_dotenv

home = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
env = home / ".env"
content = "HERMES_TEST_KEY=hello_utf16\nSECOND_KEY=world\n"
env.write_bytes(codecs.BOM_UTF16_LE + content.encode("utf-16-le"))

os.environ.pop("HERMES_TEST_KEY", None)
os.environ.pop("SECOND_KEY", None)
load_hermes_dotenv(hermes_home=home)

print("canonical:", repr(os.environ.get("HERMES_TEST_KEY")))
print("mangled  :", repr(os.environ.get("\ufffd\ufffdHERMES_TEST_KEY")))
print("on disk  :", env.read_bytes()[:40].hex())
```

### Observed before fix

| Encoding | Canonical first key | Mangled key | On-disk after load |
|----------|---------------------|-------------|--------------------|
| UTF-16-LE + BOM | `None` | `\ufffd\ufffdHERMES_TEST_KEY=hello_utf16` | rewritten: starts `ef bf bd ef bf bd...` |
| UTF-16-BE + BOM | `None` | same class of mangling | rewritten mangled |
| UTF-16-LE no BOM | loads (accidental) | n/a | often repaired via NUL strip |
| UTF-16-BE no BOM | loads (accidental) | n/a | often repaired via NUL strip |

Mangled key name (LE+BOM, after rewrite) is literally U+FFFD U+FFFD glued to the original key: `\ufffd\ufffdHERMES_TEST_KEY` with value `hello_utf16`.

## Mechanism

`_sanitize_env_file_if_needed` (was lines ~167-217 on `main`) does:

1. `open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig", errors="replace")`
2. For a UTF-16 BOM (`FF FE` / `FE FF`), those two bytes are not a UTF-8 BOM, so they become **two U+FFFD replacement characters** glued to the first key name.
3. Embedded NUL bytes (the other half of every UTF-16 code unit for ASCII) are stripped.
4. Because `sanitized != original`, the result is written back with `mkstemp` + `fsync` + `atomic_replace` as UTF-8, **permanently** storing the U+FFFD-prefixed key.

BOM-less UTF-16 of pure ASCII happens to look like NUL-padded ASCII; the existing NUL strip path accidentally "repairs" it. That is coincidence, not a design.

## Relationship to #65123 / #65124

**Sibling, not duplicate.**

| | #65123 / #65124 | This issue |
|--|-----------------|------------|
| Encoding | UTF-8 + BOM (`EF BB BF`) | UTF-16 + BOM (`FF FE` / `FE FF`) |
| Root cause | `load_dotenv(encoding="utf-8")` keeps U+FEFF on the first key | **Sanitizer** decode with `errors=replace` then **rewrite** |
| Disk mutation | No (load-time only) | **Yes** - file permanently mangled |
| Fix surface | `_load_dotenv_with_fallback` (+ send_cmd) | `_sanitize_env_file_if_needed` |

#65248 is UTF-8 BOM only in sanitize (related but not UTF-16).

Cross-link: #65123

## Environment

- Python: 3.11 (venv `python3.11`)
- hermes-agent: 0.18.2 (`pyproject.toml`)
- python-dotenv: 1.2.2
- OS: macOS (Darwin arm64)

## Platform honesty

Repro is **byte-level emulation** of Notepad "Unicode" / UTF-16-LE+BOM and UTF-16-BE+BOM (and BOM-less variants). PowerShell 5.1 and Notepad were **not** executed on a Windows host in this run.

## Expected behavior

- UTF-16 (with BOM) `.env` should load the first key under its **canonical** name.
- On-disk file should be rewritten as **clean UTF-8** (no BOM, no U+FFFD), or left untouched if the encoding is unsupported (e.g. UTF-32: refuse-to-mangle).
- Never persist `errors=replace` garbage back to disk.

[Bug]%20_resolve_task_provider_model%20ignores%20key_env%20field%20in%20auxiliary%20task%20config%20%E2%86%92%20vision/compression%20401

## Summary

`_resolve_task_provider_model()` in `agent/auxiliary_client.py` reads `api_key` from the auxiliary task config but **never reads `key_env`** (or `api_key_env`). When a user configures an auxiliary task with `key_env` instead of a plaintext `api_key`, the resolved API key is `None`, and requests are sent with the `"no-key-required"` placeholder → `401 AuthenticationError` on every call.

## Reproduction

```yaml
# ~/.hermes/config.yaml
auxiliary:
  vision:
    provider: custom
    model: qwen3.7-plus
    base_url: https://coding.dashscope.aliyuncs.com/v1
    key_env: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY      # ← this field is NEVER parsed
    timeout: 120
```

```bash
# .env has the key
DASHSCOPE_API_KEY=sk-sp-xxxxxxxxxxxx
```

```python
# vision_analyze tool fails every time:
# openai.AuthenticationError: Error code: 401 - {'error': {'code': 'invalid_api_key', ...}}
```

## Root Cause

`agent/auxiliary_client.py`, function `_resolve_task_provider_model()` (line ~5888):

```python
cfg_api_key = str(task_config.get("api_key", "")).strip() or None
# ← key_env is never consulted here
cfg_api_mode = str(task_config.get("api_mode", "")).strip() or None
```

The `key_env` field **is** correctly parsed in two other places in the same file:
- `_fallback_entry_api_key()` (L3987) — reads `key_env`/`api_key_env`
- named custom provider resolution (L4721) — reads `key_env`/`api_key_env`

But the top-level auxiliary task config resolution path in `_resolve_task_provider_model()` does not.

## Impact

Any auxiliary task (`vision`, `compression`, `web_extract`, `session_search`) configured with `key_env` instead of inline `api_key` will fail with 401. This is the documented/recommended way to configure credentials (keeping secrets in `.env`, not `config.yaml`), so users following best practices hit this bug.

Related issues:
- #9318 — similar symptom (no-key-required fallback) but different root cause (wants to inherit `model.api_key`)
- #16254 — mentions `key_env never parsed in aux config` as a side note

## Fix

Add `key_env` resolution in `_resolve_task_provider_model()` right after reading `cfg_api_key`:

```python
cfg_api_key = str(task_config.get("api_key", "")).strip() or None
# Resolve key_env → env var if api_key is not set directly
if not cfg_api_key:
    cfg_key_env = str(task_config.get("key_env") or task_config.get("api_key_env") or "").strip()
    if cfg_key_env:
        cfg_api_key = os.getenv(cfg_key_env, "").strip() or None
cfg_api_mode = str(task_config.get("api_mode", "")).strip() or None
```

This mirrors the same `key_env`/`api_key_env` fallback pattern already used in `_fallback_entry_api_key()` and named custom provider resolution.

- OS: macOS 15.5 (Apple Silicon M4 Max)
- Config: `auxiliary.vision.provider: custom` with `key_env: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY`

## Bug Description

`agent/system_prompt.py` (`build_system_prompt_parts`) describes the agent's own filesystem layout using hardcoded `~/.hermes/...` literals rather than deriving it from `get_hermes_home()`. Under any non-default `HERMES_HOME` — the Docker default `/opt/data`, or profile mode where `HERMES_HOME` is `<root>/profiles/<name>` — the system prompt states paths that **do not exist**, and the agent believes them.

Notably, `hermes_constants.get_hermes_home()` already documents itself as the fix:
> Reads HERMES_HOME env var, falls back to `~/.hermes`. **This is the single source of truth — all other copies should import this.**

The tools (`browser_tool.py`, `browser_camofox*.py`, …) and the cross-profile guard (`agent/file_safety.py`) already import it. `agent/system_prompt.py` is the outlier that hardcodes.

1. Run the gateway with a non-default home, e.g. Docker `-e HERMES_HOME=/opt/data`.

The system prompt names the agent's real directories, derived from `get_hermes_home()` / `get_default_hermes_root()`, so the agent looks in the right place.

The prompt hardcodes `~/.hermes/...`. In our container (`HERMES_HOME=/opt/data`, profile mode):

```
EXISTS   /opt/data/profiles/coder          <- the real profile dir (== get_hermes_home())
MISSING  /opt/data/.hermes/profiles/coder  <- where the prompt sends the agent
MISSING  /root/.hermes                      <- literal ~/.hermes
```

The failure is independent of how `~` expands — neither `/root/.hermes` nor `/opt/data/.hermes` exists. The only correct value is `get_hermes_home()`.

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory) — specifically system-prompt assembly. Platform-agnostic (affects every profile/adapter, not a specific messaging platform).

`agent/system_prompt.py` hardcodes the default layout in four places inside `build_system_prompt_parts`:

+export const DEFAULT_BACKEND_READY_TIMEOUT_MS = 45_000
+export const DEFAULT_BACKEND_READY_POLL_MS = 500
+// A cold backend can stall its event loop for tens of seconds while Windows
+// scans and byte-compiles the gateway import tree. At the default 15s socket
+// timeout only three probes fit in the budget; a short one keeps retrying
+// across the stall. Health only — the legacy /api/status fallback is genuinely
+// slow to answer and keeps the caller's default timeout.
+export const DEFAULT_HEALTH_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000
+
+type FetchPublicJson = (url: string, options?: { timeoutMs?: number }) => Promise<unknown>
+type FetchJson = (url: string, token?: string | null, options?: { timeoutMs?: number }) => Promise<unknown>
+
+export interface HermesReadyOptions {
+  fetchPublicJson: FetchPublicJson
+  fetchJson: FetchJson
+  token?: string | null
+  signal?: AbortSignal
+  timeoutMs?: number
+  pollMs?: number
+  healthProbeTimeoutMs?: number
+  sleep?: (ms: number) => Promise<void>
+  now?: () => number
+}
+
+export function isMissingHealthEndpointError(error: unknown): boolean {
+  const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error ?? '')
+
+  return /^404:/.test(message) || message.includes('endpoint is likely missing')
+}
+
+function supersededError() {
+  const error: any = new Error('SSH bootstrap was superseded by newer connection settings.')
+  error.kind = 'superseded'
+
+  return error
+}
+
+export async function waitForHermesReady(baseUrl: string, options: HermesReadyOptions): Promise<void> {
+  const timeoutMs = options.timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_BACKEND_READY_TIMEOUT_MS
+  const pollMs = options.pollMs ?? DEFAULT_BACKEND_READY_POLL_MS
+  const healthProbeTimeoutMs = options.healthProbeTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_HEALTH_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS
+  const now = options.now ?? Date.now
+  const signal = options.signal
+
+  const sleep =
+    options.sleep ??
+    (ms =>
+      new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
+        const timer = setTimeout(resolve, ms)
+        signal?.addEventListener(
+          'abort',
+          () => {
+            clearTimeout(timer)
+            reject(supersededError())
+          },
+          { once: true }
+        )
+      }))
+
+  const base = baseUrl.replace(/\/+$/, '')
+  const deadline = now() + timeoutMs
+  let lastError: unknown = null
+  let useStatusFallback = false
+
+  while (now() < deadline) {
+    if (signal?.aborted) {
+      throw supersededError()
+    }
+
+    try {
+      if (useStatusFallback) {
+        await options.fetchJson(`${base}/api/status`, options.token)
+      } else {
+        await options.fetchPublicJson(`${base}/api/health`, { timeoutMs: healthProbeTimeoutMs })
+      }
+
+      return
+    } catch (error) {
+      lastError = error
+
+      // Only an explicitly missing route means the backend predates
+      // /api/health; timeouts and server errors keep polling health.
+      if (!useStatusFallback && isMissingHealthEndpointError(error)) {
+        useStatusFallback = true
+
+        continue
+      }
+
+      await sleep(pollMs)
+    }
+  }
+
+  const detail = lastError instanceof Error ? lastError.message : 'timeout'
+  throw new Error(`Hermes backend did not become ready: ${detail}`)
+}

# OpenRouter requests don't send `session_id` → no sticky routing / prompt caching for paid multi-turn
## Summary
Hermes does not forward `session_id` to OpenRouter on chat requests. This disables OpenRouter's sticky-routing + prompt-caching for multi-turn agent loops.
## Evidence
- Searched `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/agent/auxiliary_client.py` for `session_id|extra_body|session|sticky` → 0 matches.
- `tools/openrouter_client.py` only builds the client via the centralized router; no `extra_body` injection.
- Hermes does per-conversation prefix caching internally (per AGENTS.md), but that's a separate layer from OpenRouter's API-level `session_id`.
## Impact
For paid OpenRouter models (e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` via OpenRouter), multi-turn agent loops hit a *cold* provider on turn 2 → full input price, no cache reuse. The OpenRouter blog recommends `session_id` to pin the session to the provider holding the warm cache from turn 1. Free `:free` tier is unaffected (volatile routing).
## Proposed fix (~5 lines)
In the OpenRouter request path, inject a stable-per-conversation id:
```python
extra_body = {"session_id": <stable conversation_id>}
```
where `conversation_id` is already available internally and stable for the life of the conversation.
## Docs reference
https://openrouter.ai/blog/tutorials/prompt-caching-sticky-routing/
## Environment
- Hermes Agent (Nous Research), macOS
- Provider: OpenRouter (paid models used sporadically; `:free` daily)
- Repro: any multi-turn conversation using a paid OpenRouter model → check `cached_tokens` in usage response → stays 0 / low across turns because requests land on different provider endpoints (no sticky routing).

Docker image ships WAL-reset-vulnerable SQLite (Debian trixie libsqlite3 3.46.1) — no fixed-SQLite path for image installs (parity with #70200/#70186)

The official image (`FROM debian:13.4`, apt `python3`, venv via `uv sync` on the system interpreter) dynamically links `libsqlite3-0 3.46.1-7+deb13u1`, which `hermes doctor` itself flags as vulnerable to the WAL-reset corruption bug (https://sqlite.org/wal.html#walresetbug, fixed 3.51.3+, backports 3.50.7 / 3.44.6). Debian trixie carries no backport (its latest changelog entry, 2026-01-22, only addresses CVE-2025-7709), so `docker pull` + recreate keeps shipping the vulnerable library indefinitely.

#70200 / #70186 repair managed (uv / python-build-standalone) installs, but image installs have no equivalent path; the #70055 DELETE-mode gate protects only NEW shared DBs, so pre-existing WAL databases (`kanban.db`, `state.db`) on busy multi-worker boards still ride the vulnerable checkpoint path — we have observed live `kanban.db` corruption fences on 0.19.0 under concurrent-worker load.

**Request:** bake a fixed SQLite (>= 3.51.3; #70200 targets 3.53.1) into the published image — e.g. compile the pinned autoconf amalgamation into `/usr/local/lib/<multiarch>` ahead of the distro lib, or install a fixed `libsqlite3-0` — and/or document an endorsed override for derived images.

Happy to share our derived-image layer (pinned 3.53.3 build with SHA3 verification and build-time version/FTS5 asserts) as a reference.
